To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
chronic exercise can compensate for insulin resistance induced in rats by a high fat fed diet.

1) exercise is beneficial in the treatment of insulin resistant states such as obesity and type II diabetes and 2) different processes appear to be responsible for the development of insulin resistance in muscle, and for its correction by exercise.

exercise training prevents the high fat diet induced reduction in whole body glucose utilization, but does not prevent the high fat diet-induced reduction in insulin action on individual skeletal muscles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of physical activity on glucose metabolism in normal and abnormal states.
the effects of exercise on insulin resistance and the development of type 2 diabetes mellitus.
the effects of diet and exercise on the development of insulin resistance in the skeletal muscle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chronic exercise prevents insulin resistant development in HFF rats, but this is a compensation rather than correction of the diet induced insulin resistant defect.
chronic exercise is an effective treatment for high fat diet induced peripheral insulin resistance, but that it is not a cure.
chronic exercise can compensate for, but not correct, insulin resistance in HFF rats.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chronic exercise can compensate for the peripheral insulin resistance induced by high fat feeding.
chronic exercise can ameliorate insulin resistance induced by high fat diet, but the mechanisms are not the same as in insulin resistance due to obesity.
exercise training is a potent intervention in the development of insulin resistance in HFF rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
regular exercise is beneficial to counteract high fat diet induced peripheral insulin resistance.
physical activity is beneficial and can counteract insulin resistance.
exercise can be a powerful countermeasure to diet-induced insulin resistance.
